title: Diagnose Ignition Gateway Performance Using the Performance Page
summary: Use the Ignition gateway performance page in a web browser to review Memory Trend, CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events while investigating an OptiSweep system issue. The memory chart can provide evidence of a spike followed by a drop to 0, but the Gateway chart alone does not establish the underlying application fault.
when_to_use: Use the Ignition gateway performance page when investigating an OptiSweep system issue and Gateway-level memory, response, or slow-response behavior needs to be checked.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a Perspective diagnostic; the source distinguishes the Ignition gateway from Perspective.
Do not treat the Gateway performance chart alone as proof of the underlying application fault or as the sole explanation for a reported system symptom.
Do not use this procedure as a service restart procedure; the supplied evidence does not provide a complete named service restart workflow.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support accesses the Ignition gateway performance page and interprets the displayed Gateway-level indicators.
L2_support correlates the displayed evidence with the reported system behavior and escalates when the page cannot be opened or the evidence does not explain the symptom.
safety_notes: This is an observation-only diagnostic procedure based on the supplied evidence; no production stop or physical intervention is specified.
A memory spike followed by a drop to 0 is an indicator associated with a crash, not proof of the underlying application cause.

access_required: L2_support access to the Ignition gateway
Web browser access to the Ignition gateway
system_preconditions: The Ignition gateway is reachable through the web browser.

visual_references.description: Ignition gateway performance page showing the browser path, Memory Trend, CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events.

steps.title: Open the Ignition gateway performance page
steps.purpose: Access the live Ignition gateway performance indicators used for the diagnostic.
steps.instruction: In a web browser, open the Ignition gateway and navigate to `/web/status/sys.performance?2`. Confirm that the page is the Ignition gateway performance page, not Perspective.
steps.expected_result: The Ignition gateway performance page opens and displays Gateway performance sections, including Memory Trend, CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events.
steps.healthy_condition: The Ignition gateway performance page loads and the named performance sections are visible.
steps.failure_condition: The page cannot be opened, does not load the named Gateway performance sections, or the displayed interface is Perspective rather than the Ignition gateway.

actions.label: Open performance page
actions.exact_action: Open the Ignition gateway in a web browser and navigate to `/web/status/sys.performance?2`.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to deeper Ignition or system troubleshooting if the performance page cannot be opened.

source_evidence.quote: This is just the gateway and not perspective.
Ignition can be accessed through the web browser. http://localhost:8088/web/status/sys.performance?2

steps.title: Review the Memory Trend
steps.purpose: Identify the memory behavior associated with a possible Gateway crash.
steps.instruction: On the Ignition gateway performance page, inspect the Memory Trend chart. Determine whether the displayed memory usage shows a spike followed by a drop to 0.
steps.expected_result: The current Memory Trend behavior is observable, including whether a spike followed by a drop to 0 is present.
steps.healthy_condition: The Memory Trend does not show the supplied crash-associated spike-then-zero pattern during the period being reviewed.
steps.failure_condition: The Memory Trend shows a memory spike followed by a drop to 0, which is evidence associated with a Gateway crash.

actions.label: Inspect Memory Trend
actions.exact_action: Review the Memory Trend chart and check for a memory spike followed by a drop to 0.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate when a memory spike followed by a drop to 0 is observed, especially if the related system symptom persists.

source_evidence.quote: If you had a crash ... this would show you that the memory spiked and then dropped to 0.

steps.title: Check response and slow-event indicators
steps.purpose: Review the other live Gateway performance indicators that may provide supporting evidence.
steps.instruction: On the Ignition gateway performance page, inspect CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events. Read the displayed values and determine whether Recent Slow Response Events contains entries or displays `No events to display`.
steps.expected_result: The displayed CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events state are observable.
steps.healthy_condition: The performance sections load and Recent Slow Response Events displays `No events to display`, or the displayed values do not show an abnormal response condition during the review.
steps.failure_condition: A response indicator is unavailable or abnormal, or Recent Slow Response Events contains entries that require correlation with the reported system behavior.

actions.label: Inspect performance indicators
actions.exact_action: Check CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to deeper Ignition or system troubleshooting if the displayed response evidence does not explain the reported system behavior.

source_evidence.quote: CPU Trend ... Memory Trend ... System Response ... Current Response Time ... Recent Slow Response Events ... No events to display

steps.title: Record and interpret the observed Gateway evidence
steps.purpose: Preserve the observed memory, response, and event state without overstating what the Gateway chart proves.
steps.instruction: Record the currently displayed Memory Trend pattern, CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events state. Correlate these observations with the reported OptiSweep system behavior, and do not conclude that the Ignition gateway is the sole cause from the chart alone.
steps.expected_result: The live Gateway observations and their relationship to the reported symptom are captured, with any uncertainty or unexplained symptom identified for further troubleshooting.
steps.healthy_condition: The observations are available for correlation and no unsupported conclusion is made about the underlying application fault.
steps.failure_condition: The Gateway evidence does not explain the reported symptom, or the chart is treated as definitive proof of the application fault.

actions.label: Capture diagnostic observations
actions.exact_action: Record the currently displayed memory pattern, response information, and event state without treating the Gateway chart alone as proof of the underlying application fault.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate to deeper Ignition or system troubleshooting when the observed memory or response evidence does not explain the reported system behavior.
Do not close the investigation solely because the Gateway chart does not show the crash-associated pattern.

success_criteria: The Ignition gateway performance page opens in a web browser.
Memory Trend, CPU Trend, System Response, Current Response Time, and Recent Slow Response Events are reviewed.
The memory pattern and response/event observations are captured.
Any spike followed by a drop to 0 is identified as crash-associated evidence rather than definitive proof of root cause.
The Gateway chart is not treated as the sole explanation for the reported system behavior.
healthy_conditions: The Ignition gateway performance page loads and displays the named performance sections.
Memory Trend does not show the supplied spike-followed-by-zero pattern during the reviewed period.
Recent Slow Response Events displays `No events to display`, when that is the live displayed state.
The displayed response information is available for correlation with the reported symptom.
failure_conditions: The Ignition gateway performance page cannot be opened.
The performance page does not display the expected Gateway performance sections.
Memory Trend shows a spike followed by a drop to 0.
Recent Slow Response Events contains entries or response indicators show behavior requiring further investigation.
The observed Gateway evidence does not explain the reported system behavior.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to deeper Ignition or system troubleshooting if the performance page cannot be opened.
Escalate when a memory spike followed by a drop to 0 is observed, especially if the related system symptom persists.
Escalate when the observed memory or response evidence does not explain the reported system behavior.
Do not conclude that the Ignition gateway is the sole cause from the performance chart alone.
